Hena
HEE-nah
proper noun
Hebrew Hena, a city of the region the Assyrian had conquered; named by the Rabshakeh in his taunt against Jerusalem, that no god had delivered these cities from his master’s hand.

📖 Biblical Definition

Hena is a name flung out in a blasphemer’s boast. When the Rabshakeh of Assyria stood before the walls of Jerusalem, he numbered the fallen cities like trophies and mocked the God of Judah with them: “Where are the gods of Hamath, and of Arpad? where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? have they delivered Samaria out of mine hand?” (2Ki 18:34). The same names return in Sennacherib’s letter: “Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivah?” (2Ki 19:13). The Assyrian’s reasoning was simple and profane: the idols of Hena did not save Hena, therefore the God of Jerusalem cannot save Jerusalem. But he had confounded the living God with the dead gods of the heathen, and that is the sin of every boaster who measures the Almighty by the impotence of idols. The gods of Hena were nothing, wood and stone that could not deliver their own city; but the LORD made the heavens, and He is not as the gods of the nations. Hezekiah spread the blasphemous letter before the LORD, and in one night the angel of the LORD smote the camp of Assyria. Hena stands forever as the boaster’s miscalculation: the God who was mocked among the idols of the conquered cities is the God who saves His own for His own name’s sake.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A city the Assyrian boasted his gods had destroyed, named in the Rabshakeh’s taunt against Jerusalem (2Ki 18:34; 19:13); a witness that the living God is not as the idols of the conquered nations.

HENA, a city conquered by Assyria.

Named by the Rabshakeh in his taunt against Jerusalem (2Ki 18:34).

Its gods did not deliver it out of the Assyrian’s hand.

The boaster confounded the living God with the idols of the heathen.

A witness that the LORD is not as the gods of Hena.

📖 Key Scripture

2Ki 18:34 — "Where are the gods of Hamath, and of Arpad? where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? have they delivered Samaria out of mine hand?"

2Ki 19:13 — "Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivah?"

Psa 96:5 — "For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the LORD made the heavens."

Isa 37:13 — "Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arphad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah?"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The city named in the Assyrian’s taunt; the entry names the blasphemy of the boaster who confounds the living God with the dead idols of the conquered nations.

expand to see more

Hena is remembered as a name in a blasphemer’s mouth. The Rabshakeh counted her among the cities whose gods had failed and reasoned that the God of Jerusalem must fail as well, having confounded the LORD who made the heavens with the wood and stone of the heathen.

The genuine sin here is plainly named: it is the blasphemy of the proud conqueror who measures the Almighty by the impotence of idols. The gods of Hena were nothing, and could not deliver their own city; but the LORD is the living God, and He is not as the gods of the nations. Hezekiah spread the boaster’s letter before Him, and in one night the camp of Assyria was smitten. Let no man reckon the God of Scripture among the idols that could not save Hena; He saves His own for His own name’s sake.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Hena, a conquered city of the Assyrian taunt, paired with Ivah; its gods a byword for idols that could not deliver.

expand to see more

Hena — Hebrew Hena, a city subdued by Assyria.

Named with Ivah and Sepharvaim in the Rabshakeh’s taunt.

Its gods could not deliver it out of the Assyrian’s hand (2Ki 18:34).

Repeated in Sennacherib’s letter to Hezekiah (2Ki 19:13).

A byword for the dead idols that the boaster set against the LORD.

Usage

"The Rabshakeh mocked Jerusalem with the gods of Hena."

"Where are the gods of Hena and Ivah, said the boaster."

"The gods of Hena could not save it, but the LORD saved Zion."
